title: What If You Ate One of the World's Hottest Peppers?

scenes.text: What if you ate the Carolina Reaper? The pain isn't the scary part.
It was once the world's hottest pepper, rated about 1.5 million Scoville units. A jalapeno tops out near 10,000.
In one 2018 case, a man ate one at a contest. Dry heaves came first, then pain in the back of his head.
Over the next few days he had several thunderclap headaches, brief bursts of severe pain peaking within a minute.
A CT scan showed several arteries in his brain had narrowed. Doctors diagnosed reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome.
He recovered without treatment. Five weeks later his arteries were normal again. Doctors say the pepper likely triggered it.

description:
What if you ate the Carolina Reaper?
A 2018 case report in BMJ Case Reports described a man who developed thunderclap headaches after eating one. He recovered fully, and doctors believe the pepper likely triggered it. This is one reported case, not medical advice.
